title: Features: Useful Clues
outcome: By the end, I can choose task-relevant features and avoid a clue created after the decision.
scenario: A fictional shelf accepts a craft box only if width is at most 6 cm and height at most 4 cm.
given: A green acceptance sticker is attached only after the shelf check.

steps.label: Apply both limits
steps.detail: P and S fit; Q fails width; R fails height.

steps.label: Reject a shortcut
steps.detail: The later sticker cannot be an input available before checking.

explanation: Comparing P with Q isolates width; comparing P with R isolates height. Comparing P with S changes pattern while both remain accepted. Under this declared policy, pattern is not a deciding feature. A later acceptance sticker leaks the very answer the system should produce.

counterfactual.change: Change Q’s width to 6 without changing its height.
counterfactual.reason: Both dimensions now meet their including equality limits; stripe pattern does not change the rule.

student_task: Point to the pair that tests pattern, then explain why the sticker is a bad early input.
teacher_answer: P and S test pattern. The sticker is attached after the decision, so it is unavailable when a new box must be checked.
project_evidence: Choose sorter features that exist at decision time and actually connect to the stated classroom requirement.
limits: These comparisons establish the written shelf rule, not the importance of pattern for unrelated tasks.
review_note: New fictional worked case reviewed against the weekly topic and reserved independent assessment. Keep that assessment separate; this picture is supported practice.
